name: running
why: No marker at all is the ordinary state of an app.

name: stopped, in a record with CRLF line endings
why: A CR is invisible in an editor. The shell strips it with `tr -d '\r'` and bufio.Scanner strips it for free; without either the value is "1\r", which is not "1", and the two readers disagree about the same file.

name: stopped, with a later line contradicting it
why: First wins, which is what readState does and what the shell's `head -n 1` does. A reader that took the last line would disagree with every other reader of these records.

name: a record with a similarly named key
why: A key that merely ends in STOPPED is a different key. The shell anchors with `^`; the Go side splits on `=` and compares a whole key.

name: a hand-written STOPPED=0
why: ClearStopped removes the key rather than writing a 0, so a 0 only ever arrives from a person -- and reading it as a stop takes their "no" for a yes.

name: a value that merely contains a 1
why: Exactly "1", not "contains a 1". A hand-edited record can pick up a trailing space, and both readers must make the same nothing of it.
